reasons: 1. What it tells me (residential cleaning owner): when a quote text comes in at night, paste it into free Gemini with this prompt, cut the extra question, put my price in and send it myself before my first job, not at lunch.

2. Stop: yes. The real 11 pm request with the reply already written is on screen by 2.5 s, the cover '11 pm quote. / Reply in 7 seconds.' is my phone at night, and 'One thing's wrong' gives me a reason to stay. Answered at line 5 ('It asked two questions'), late enough to hold me.

3. Send: yes, to whoever answers my quote texts; one prompt and one rule ('a price and one question') is easy to pass on. Save: yes, the prompt is short, exact, has a [your price] slot, is held on its own card and repeated word for word in the caption. Follow or link: no; one good tip, and 'Free tools for trade owners: link in bio' gives no specific reason to tap. Not blocking.

4. Hype, fake urgency, pitch, slop, robotic: none found. Cost said ('It's free.', backed by the plan page), time said honestly as the reply's time ('this reply took under seven seconds', 6.6 s run), the flaw shown and fixed ('Cut one, add your price, send it yourself'). No claim that AI books jobs. The [matter-of-fact] and [confident] tags fit the lines; nothing sounds read off a vendor sheet.

5. Unclear to a stranger (not blocking): line 4 'Paste their text into Gemini with this prompt.' names the prompt but never says it, so the viewer depends on the card; 4 s is enough to see it and decide to save, not enough to read about 130 characters at phone size. Fix (design side, not script): keep the prompt card up through 'It's free.' and into the start of line 5, or hold it longer, and make sure the reply card comes back on 'It asked two questions' so 'It' has a referent. Minor: line 3 '26% within an hour' next to the button 'before your first job' (about 8 hours after 11 pm) leaves a sharp owner asking 'so I am still slow?'; 'only' makes it a stake that a morning reply beats lunch, so it holds.

6. Trust: yes. The reply is labelled real with model, API and date; the caption says the free app uses a lighter model so mine will read differently; the price stays a slot; the story is labelled EXAMPLE; Jobber's number is said as Jobber's. Small note: cover 'Reply in 7 seconds' is model time, the voice's 'this reply took' keeps it honest.

7. The bar. C1 met: the hook shows the object (the 11 pm quote request) and line 2 says the cost, 'They've booked someone else.' (a lost job), with Jobber's 'only twenty-six percent' as the stake. S1 met: line 3 'No price, no question, so nothing to text back.' is the why, restated as the rule in line 6 ('Every quote reply needs a price and one question'). C3 met: the exact prompt on the held save card (brief: 4 s or more from 'with this prompt', above the 3 s floor) and in the caption. S3 met: 'Send that reply before your first job.' plus 'Cut one, add your price, send it yourself' is one thing I can do this week in minutes.
